<transformation>
The input is treated as a tile map. The output is NxM times larger than the input (where the input is N rows x M cols). Each input cell at (BR, BC) with a non-zero value causes a copy of the full input to be placed in the corresponding NxM block of the output (at rows BR*N .. BR*N+N-1, cols BC*M .. BC*M+M-1). Each input cell with value 0 produces an all-zero block at that position.
</transformation>

<asp>
% Count distinct row/col indices — equals grid dimensions for 0-indexed inputs
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{R : input(R, _, _)}.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{C : input(_, C, _)}.

% Output is NR*NR rows and NC*NC cols (input tiled by itself)
output_cell(R, C) :-
    input(BR, BC, _), input(DR, DC, _),
    n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
    R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC.

1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Non-zero block: the sub-cell must equal the input value at the relative position
:- input(BR, BC, V), V != 0,
   input(DR, DC, TileColor),
   n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
   R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC,
   output(R, C, ActualColor), ActualColor != TileColor.

% Zero block: every sub-cell must be 0
:- input(BR, BC, 0),
   input(DR, DC, _),
   n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
   R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC,
   output(R, C, ActualColor), ActualColor != 0.
</asp>

The output is the same size as the input. Color-3 cells are unchanged. Non-3 cells (value 0) that are enclosed by color-3 walls — i.e., cannot reach the grid boundary via 4-connected movement through non-3 cells — are filled with color 4. All other non-3 cells remain 0.

<asp>
% Output has the same dimensions as the input
output_cell(R, C) :- input(R, C, _).
1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Grid boundary coordinates
min_row(R) :- R = #min{Row : input(Row, _, _)}.
max_row(R) :- R = #max{Row : input(Row, _, _)}.
min_col(C) :- C = #min{Col : input(_, Col, _)}.
max_col(C) :- C = #max{Col : input(_, Col, _)}.

% 4-connected adjacency offsets
delta(0,1). delta(0,-1). delta(1,0). delta(-1,0).

% Non-3 cells on the grid boundary are reachable from outside
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, min_row(Rmin), R = Rmin.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, max_row(Rmax), R = Rmax.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, min_col(Cmin), C = Cmin.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, max_col(Cmax), C = Cmax.

% Flood-fill outward through non-3 cells
outside(R2, C2) :-
    outside(R1, C1), delta(DR, DC),
    R2 = R1+DR, C2 = C1+DC,
    input(R2, C2, V), V != 3.

% Color-3 cells stay 3
:- input(R, C, 3), output(R, C, Color), Color != 3.

% Outside non-3 cells stay 0
:- outside(R, C), output(R, C, Color), Color != 0.

% Interior non-3 cells (enclosed by 3s, not reachable from boundary) become 4
:- input(R, C, 0), not outside(R, C), output(R, C, Color), Color != 4.
</asp>

% Determine bounding rectangle of cells with colour 4
minR(R) :- R = #min{R : input(R, _, 4)}.
maxR(R) :- R = #max{R : input(R, _, 4)}.
minC(C) :- C = #min{C : input(_, C, 4)}.
maxC(C) :- C = #max{C : input(_, C, 4)}.

% Dimensions of the rectangle
N(N) :- N = maxR - minR + 1.
M(M) :- M = maxC - minC + 1.

% Map each input cell to a cell of the output rectangle
out(Rc, Cc) :- input(R, C, _),
    R = minR + Rc,
    C = minC + Cc,
    Rc >= 0,
    Rc < N,
    Cc >= 0,
    Cc < M.

% Corners become colour 4
output(Rc, Cc, 4) :- out(Rc, Cc), Rc = 0, Cc = 0.
output(Rc, Cc, 4) :- out(Rc, Cc), Rc = 0, Cc = M-1.
output(Rc, Cc, 4) :- out(Rc, Cc), Rc = N-1, Cc = 0.
output(Rc, Cc, 4) :- out(Rc, Cc), Rc = N-1, Cc = M-1.

% Interior cells: colour depends on nearest corner (ties: TL → 3, TR → 2, BL → 1, BR → 0)
output(Rc, Cc, 3) :- out(Rc, Cc),
    Rc != 0, Rc != N-1, Cc != 0, Cc != M-1,
    Rc + Cc <= Rc + (M-1 - Cc),
    Rc + Cc <= (N-1 - Rc) + Cc,
    Rc + Cc <= (N-1 - Rc) + (M-1 - Cc).

output(Rc, Cc, 2) :- out(Rc, Cc),
    Rc != 0, Rc != N-1, Cc != 0, Cc != M-1,
    Rc + (M-1 - Cc) <= Rc + Cc,
    Rc + (M-1 - Cc) <= (N-1 - Rc) + Cc,
    Rc + (M-1 - Cc) <= (N-1 - Rc) + (M-1 - Cc).

output(Rc, Cc, 1) :- out(Rc, Cc),
    Rc != 0, Rc != N-1, Cc != 0, Cc != M-1,
    (N-1 - Rc) + Cc <= Rc + Cc,
    (N-1 - Rc) + Cc <= Rc + (M-1 - Cc),
    (N-1 - Rc) + Cc <= (N-1 - Rc) + (M-1 - Cc).

% -----------------------------------------------------------------
%  The transformation:  the 4‑cells are the four corners of a
%  rectangle.  All other cells are coloured according to which
%  of the four corners of that rectangle is closest (ties are
%  broken by the order TL‑TR‑BL‑BR).  TL → 3, TR → 2, BL → 1,
%  BR → 0.  The rectangle is defined by the rows/cols that contain
%  a 4‑cell.
% -----------------------------------------------------------------

% ---- 1.  Determine the rectangle spanned by the 4‑cells -----------------
%   (the 4‑cells are the outermost non‑zero cells)
maxRow4(R) :- R = #max{R : input(R, _, 4)}.
maxCol4(C) :- C = #max{C : input(_, C, 4)}.
minRow4(R) :- R = #min{R : input(R, _, 4)}.
minCol4(C) :- C = #min{C : input(_, C, 4)}.

%   rectangle size
N(N)  :- N = maxRow4 - minRow4 + 1.   % number of rows
M(M)  :- M = maxCol4 - minCol4 + 1.   % number of columns

% -----------------------------------------------------------------
%   2.  Map every input cell to the output rectangle
%      (subtract the left/top margin of the 4‑cells)
% -----------------------------------------------------------------
output(Rout,Cout,Color) :- input(R,C,V),
    Rout = R - minRow4,
    Cout = C - minCol4,

    % ---- corners become colour 4 ------------------------------------
    (Rout = 0,            Cout = 0)      -> Color = 4;
    (Rout = 0,            Cout = M-1)    -> Color = 4;
    (Rout = N-1,            Cout = 0)    -> Color = 4;
    (Rout = N-1,            Cout = M-1)   -> Color = 4;

    % ---- interior cells – choose nearest corner --------------------
    (Rout != 0,            Cout != 0,
     Rout != N-1,          Cout != M-1),

    let dTL = Rout + Cout,
    dTL <= Rout + (M-1 - Cout),
    dTL <= (N-1 - Rout) + Cout,
    dTL <= (N-1 - Rout) + (M-1 - Cout) -> Color = 3;   % TL → 3

    (Rout != 0,            Cout != 0,
     Rout != N-1,          Cout != M-1),

    let dTR = Rout + (M-1 - Cout),
    dTR <= Rout + Cout,
    dTR <= (N-1 - Rout) + Cout,
    dTR <= (N-1 - Rout) + (M-1 - Cout) -> Color = 2;   % TR → 2

    (Rout != 0,            Cout != 0,
     Rout != N-1,          Cout != M-1),

    let dBL = (N-1 - Rout) + Cout,
    dBL <= Rout + Cout,
    dBL <= Rout + (M-1 - Cout),
    dBL <= (N-1 - Rout) + (M-1 - Cout) -> Color = 1;   % BL → 1

    (Rout != 0,            Cout != 0,

    let dBR = (N-1 - Rout) + (M-1 - Cout),
    dBR <= Rout + Cout,
    dBR <= Rout + (M-1 - Cout),
    dBR <= (N-1 - Rout) + Cout,
    dBR <= (N-1 - Rout) + (M-1 - Cout) -> Color = 0;   % BR → 0

% -----------------------------------------------------------------
%  The transformation:  the 4‑cells are the four corners of a
%  rectangle.  All other cells are coloured according to which
%  of the four corners of that rectangle is closest (ties are
%  broken by the order TL‑TR‑BL‑BR).  TL → 3, TR → 2, BL → 1,
%  BR → 0.  The rectangle is defined by the rows/cols that contain
%  a 4‑cell.
% -----------------------------------------------------------------

% ---- 1.  Determine the rectangle spanned by the 4‑cells -----------------
%   (the 4‑cells are the outermost non‑zero cells)
maxRow4(R) :- R = #max{R : input(R, _, 4)}.
maxCol4(C) :- C = #max{C : input(_, C, 4)}.
minRow4(R) :- R = #min{R : input(R, _, 4)}.
minCol4(C) :- C = #min{C : input(_, C, 4)}.

%   rectangle size
N(N)  :- N = maxRow4 - minRow4 + 1.   % number of rows
M(M)  :- M = maxCol4 - minCol4 + 1.   % number of columns

% -----------------------------------------------------------------
%   2.  Map every input cell to the output rectangle
%      (subtract the left/top margin of the 4‑cells)
% -----------------------------------------------------------------
output(Rout,Cout,Color) :- input(R,C,V),
    Rout = R - minRow4,
    Cout = C - minCol4,

    % ---- corners become colour 4 ------------------------------------
    (Rout = 0,            Cout = 0)      -> Color = 4;
    (Rout = 0,            Cout = M-1)    -> Color = 4;
    (Rout = N-1,            Cout = 0)    -> Color = 4;
    (Rout = N-1,            Cout = M-1)   -> Color = 4;

    % ---- interior cells – choose nearest corner --------------------
    (Rout != 0,            Cout != 0,
     Rout != N-1,          Cout != M-1),

    let dTL = Rout + Cout,
    dTL <= Rout + (M-1 - Cout),
    dTL <= (N-1 - Rout) + Cout,
    dTL <= (N-1 - Rout) + (M-1 - Cout) -> Color = 3;   % TL → 3

    (Rout != 0,            Cout != 0,
     Rout != N-1,          Cout != M-1),

    let dTR = Rout + (M-1 - Cout),
    dTR <= Rout + Cout,
    dTR <= (N-1 - Rout) + Cout,
    dTR <= (N-1 - Rout) + (M-1 - Cout) -> Color = 2;   % TR → 2

    (Rout != 0,            Cout != 0,
     Rout != N-1,          Cout != M-1),

    let dBL = (N-1 - Rout) + Cout,
    dBL <= Rout + Cout,
    dBL <= Rout + (M-1 - Cout),
    dBL <= (N-1 - Rout) + (M-1 - Cout) -> Color = 1;   % BL → 1

    (Rout != 0,            Cout != 0,
     Rout != N-1,          Cout != M-1),

    let dBR = (N-1 - Rout) + (M-1 - Cout),
    dBR <= Rout + Cout,
    dBR <= Rout + (M-1 - Cout),
    dBR <= (N-1 - Rout) + Cout,
    dBR <= (N-1 - Rout) + (M-1 - Cout) -> Color = 0;   % BR → 0

% -----------------------------------------------------------------
%   3.  Ensure that each output position has exactly one colour
% -----------------------------------------------------------------
:- output(Rout,Cout,Col1), output(Rout,Cout,Col2), Col1 != Col2.
}

% -----------------------------------------------------------------
%  The transformation:  the 4‑cells are the four corners of a
%  rectangle.  All other cells are coloured according to which
%  of the four corners of that rectangle is closest (ties are
%  broken by the order TL‑TR‑BL‑BR).  TL → 3, TR → 2, BL → 1,
%  BR → 0.  The rectangle is defined by the rows/cols that contain
%  a 4‑cell.
% -----------------------------------------------------------------

% ---- 1.  Determine the rectangle spanned by the 4‑cells -----------------
%   (the 4‑cells are the outermost non‑zero cells)
maxRow4(R) :- R = #max{R : input(R, _, 4)}.
maxCol4(C) :- C = #max{C : input(_, C, 4)}.
minRow4(R) :- R = #min{R : input(R, _, 4)}.
minCol4(C) :- C = #min{C : input(_, C, 4)}.

%   rectangle size
N(N)  :- N = maxRow4 - minRow4 + 1.   % number of rows
M(M)  :- M = maxCol4 - minCol4 + 1.   % number of columns

% -----------------------------------------------------------------
%   2.  Map every input cell to the output rectangle
%      (subtract the left/top margin of the 4‑cells)
% -----------------------------------------------------------------
output(Rout,Cout,Color) :- input(R,C,V),
    Rout = R - minRow4,
    Cout = C - minCol4,

    % ---- corners become colour 4 ------------------------------------
    (Rout = 0,            Cout = 0)      -> Color = 4;
    (Rout = 0,            Cout = M-1)    -> Color = 4;
    (Rout = N-1,            Cout = 0)    -> Color = 4;
    (Rout = N-1,            Cout = M-1)   -> Color = 4;

    % ---- interior cells – choose nearest corner --------------------
    (Rout != 0,            Cout != 0,
     Rout != N-1,          Cout != M-1),

    let dTL = Rout + Cout,
    dTL <= Rout + (M-1 - Cout),
    dTL <= (N-1 - Rout) + Cout,
    dTL <= (N-1 - Rout) + (M-1 - Cout) -> Color = 3;   % TL → 3

    (Rout != 0,            Cout != 0,
     Rout != N-1,          Cout != M-1),

    let dTR = Rout + (M-1 - Cout),
    dTR <= Rout + Cout,
    dTR <= (N-1 - Rout) + Cout,
    dTR <= (N-1 - Rout) + (M-1 - Cout) -> Color = 2;   % TR → 2

    (Rout != 0,            Cout != 0,
     Rout != N-1,          Cout != M-1),

    let dBL = (N-1 - Rout) + Cout,
    dBL <= Rout + Cout,
    dBL <= Rout + (M-1 - Cout),
    dBL <= (N-1 - Rout) + (M-1 - Cout) -> Color = 1;   % BL → 1

    (Rout != 0,            Cout != 0,
     Rout != N-1,          Cout != M-1),

    let dBR = (N-1 - Rout) + (M-1 - Cout),
    dBR <= Rout + Cout,
    dBR <= Rout + (M-1 - Cout),
    dBR <= (N-1 - Rout) + Cout,
    dBR <= (N-1 - Rout) + (M-1 - Cout) -> Color = 0;   % BR → 0

% -----------------------------------------------------------------
%   3.  Ensure that each output position has exactly one colour
% -----------------------------------------------------------------
:- output(Rout,Cout,Col1), output(Rout,Cout,Col2), Col1 != Col2.
}
